samples.title: Lớp học trực tuyến
samples.prompt: Universities should offer online classes alongside classroom lessons. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
requirementsVi: Nêu lập trường đồng ý.
Giải thích lợi ích bằng cơ chế và ví dụ.
Bàn tính khả thi, thừa nhận giới hạn và chốt lập trường.
samples.summaryVi: Học online giúp linh hoạt giờ học; cần thảo luận và hỗ trợ để tránh học một mình.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: The proposal that universities should offer online classes alongside classroom lessons raises a useful question about online university classes. I agree with this view because it can meet a practical need. My support does not mean that every version of the proposal will work; the way it is introduced is also important.
paragraphs.noteVi: Đồng ý rõ, không khẳng định mọi cách làm đều tốt.

paragraphs.label: Lý do 1 — lợi ích
paragraphs.text: One important point in favour of the proposal is that students can fit learning around work and family responsibilities. This is possible because recorded lessons can be watched again at a convenient time. For example, a student who works in a restaurant can review a morning lecture after the evening shift. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.
paragraphs.noteVi: Học online giúp linh hoạt giờ học; cần thảo luận và hỗ trợ để tránh học một mình.

paragraphs.label: Lý do 2 — cách làm khả thi
paragraphs.text: A second reason for supporting this approach is that its difficulties can be addressed through practical changes. A practical response would be to schedule small weekly discussion groups. For example, a teacher could meet six students at a time and ask each person to explain one difficult point. This approach is useful because it deals with a specific obstacle instead of simply repeating a general message. It could first be tried on a small scale, with feedback from the people involved, and then adjusted if some needs have been overlooked.
paragraphs.noteVi: Lý do thứ hai là có cách xử lý trở ngại cụ thể.

paragraphs.label: Giới hạn và kết
paragraphs.text:
It is true that some learners may feel isolated, especially because a screen does not always make it easy to ask a quick question or form friendships. This calls for better planning rather than the complete rejection of the idea.

In conclusion, I support the view that universities should offer online classes alongside classroom lessons. The main benefit is that students can fit learning around work and family responsibilities. However, careful planning and a response to practical difficulties are needed if that benefit is to be achieved.
paragraphs.noteVi: Thừa nhận giới hạn và giữ lập trường đồng ý.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: The proposal that schools should spend more money on improving their libraries raises a useful question about school libraries. I agree with this view because it can meet a practical need. My support does not mean that every version of the proposal will work; the way it is introduced is also important.

paragraphs.label: Lý do 1 — lợi ích
paragraphs.text: One important point in favour of the proposal is that students have a quiet place to study without buying every book. This is possible because shared resources help learners whose homes are noisy or crowded. For example, two students can use a library reference book to prepare a science presentation after school. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.

paragraphs.label: Lý do 2 — cách làm khả thi
paragraphs.text: A second reason for supporting this approach is that its difficulties can be addressed through practical changes. A practical response would be to ask students for suggestions and organise short library tours. For example, a librarian could show each class where to find simple reference books and offer a weekly reading recommendation. This approach is useful because it deals with a specific obstacle instead of simply repeating a general message. It could first be tried on a small scale, with feedback from the people involved, and then adjusted if some needs have been overlooked.

It is true that new books may remain unused, especially because students need help finding material that matches their level and interests. This calls for better planning rather than the complete rejection of the idea.

In conclusion, I support the view that schools should spend more money on improving their libraries. The main benefit is that students have a quiet place to study without buying every book. However, careful planning and a response to practical difficulties are needed if that benefit is to be achieved.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: The proposal that schools should give children a small amount of useful homework raises a useful question about homework for schoolchildren. I agree with this view because it can meet a practical need. My support does not mean that every version of the proposal will work; the way it is introduced is also important.
paragraphs.noteVi: Đồng ý rõ, không khẳng định mọi cách làm đều tốt.

paragraphs.label: Lý do 1 — lợi ích
paragraphs.text: One important point in favour of the proposal is that children can practise a skill after learning it in class. This is possible because short tasks can show which steps a child still does not understand. For example, five carefully chosen maths questions can reveal whether a pupil knows how to use a new method. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.
paragraphs.noteVi: Bài tập ngắn giúp luyện đúng kỹ năng; bài quá nhiều tạo bất lợi cho trẻ thiếu chỗ học hoặc hỗ trợ.

paragraphs.text: A second reason for supporting this approach is that its difficulties can be addressed through practical changes. A practical response would be to coordinate homework and give short tasks with clear purposes. For example, teachers could agree on a weekly limit and provide time at school for pupils who need help. This approach is useful because it deals with a specific obstacle instead of simply repeating a general message. It could first be tried on a small scale, with feedback from the people involved, and then adjusted if some needs have been overlooked.

In conclusion, I support the view that schools should give children a small amount of useful homework. The main benefit is that children can practise a skill after learning it in class. However, careful planning and a response to practical difficulties are needed if that benefit is to be achieved.

The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.

This approach is useful because it deals with a specific obstacle instead of simply repeating a general message. It could first be tried on a small scale, with feedback from the people involved, and then adjusted if some needs have been overlooked.

In conclusion, I support the view that language learners should practise regularly with a study partner. The main benefit is that learners have more opportunities to speak. However, careful planning and a response to practical difficulties are needed if that benefit is to be achieved.

I agree with this view because it can meet a practical need. My support does not mean that every version of the proposal will work; the way it is introduced is also important.
paragraphs.noteVi: Đồng ý rõ, không khẳng định mọi cách làm đều tốt.

paragraphs.label: Lý do 1 — lợi ích
paragraphs.text: One important point in favour of the proposal is that adults can update skills without returning to full-time study. This is possible because short local courses can fit around work and caring responsibilities. For example, a shop assistant can attend an evening computer class to learn how to manage simple spreadsheets. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.
paragraphs.noteVi: Lớp học cho người lớn cần vừa túi tiền và phù hợp giờ làm, đi lại, chăm con.

paragraphs.label: Lý do 2 — cách làm khả thi
paragraphs.text: A second reason for supporting this approach is that its difficulties can be addressed through practical changes. A practical response would be to offer flexible schedules and simple support for attendance. For example, a centre could repeat the same lesson at two different times and provide materials for missed sessions. This approach is useful because it deals with a specific obstacle instead of simply repeating a general message. It could first be tried on a small scale, with feedback from the people involved, and then adjusted if some needs have been overlooked.
paragraphs.noteVi: Lý do thứ hai là có cách xử lý trở ngại cụ thể.

paragraphs.label: Giới hạn và kết
paragraphs.text:
It is true that people with the greatest need may still be unable to attend, especially because transport, childcare and changing work hours can create barriers. This calls for better planning rather than the complete rejection of the idea.

In conclusion, I support the view that communities should provide more affordable classes for adults. The main benefit is that adults can update skills without returning to full-time study. However, careful planning and a response to practical difficulties are needed if that benefit is to be achieved.
paragraphs.noteVi: Thừa nhận giới hạn và giữ lập trường đồng ý.
